# Temple Scroll Column 27 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 27 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 27:1 — "stoa" vs. "covered colonnade" vs. "covered walkway"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "stoa" | Preserves the Greek loan-word present in the Hebrew text |
| LOGOS | "covered colonnade" | Translates the architectural concept into English |
| PNEUMA | "covered walkway" | Accessible modern description |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "covered colonnade." Translates the concept while maintaining architectural precision. "Stoa" is too specialized; "walkway" loses the columned structure.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 27:7 — "seats" vs. "benches" / "chiefs of the fathers" vs. "heads of ancestral houses" vs. "clan leaders"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "seats... chiefs of the fathers" | Literal renderings |
| LOGOS | "benches... heads of the ancestral houses" | More precise English equivalents |
| PNEUMA | "benches... clan leaders" | Modern simplified terms |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS for both: "benches" (more specific than "seats" for stone seating) and "heads of the ancestral houses" (preserves the patrilineal structure without PNEUMA's oversimplification).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 27:7 — "officers of the congregation" vs. "officers of the assembly" vs. "community officials"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "officers of the congregation" | Traditional rendering of shotrei ha-edah |
| LOGOS | "officers of the assembly" | "Assembly" for edah |
| PNEUMA | "community officials" | Modern administrative language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "officers of the congregation." "Congregation" (edah) is the well-established English equivalent in biblical contexts, preferred over "assembly" or "community."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 27:11 — "a square all around" vs. "a square on all sides" vs. "a perfect square"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a square all around" | Literal phrasing |
| LOGOS | "form a square on all sides" | Natural English |
| PNEUMA | "a perfect square" | Adds "perfect" for emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "form a square on all sides." Consistent with the rendering established in Column 25.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 27:16 — "no one who is not of the sons of Israel" vs. "no foreigner"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "no one who is not of the sons of Israel" | Literal negative construction |
| LOGOS | "no one who is not of the sons of Israel" | Same as EMET |
| PNEUMA | "no foreigner — only the sons of Israel" | Splits into positive and negative statement |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS. The original negative construction is important: the text defines eligibility by Israelite descent, not by foreignness. PNEUMA's "foreigner" introduces an ethnic category not present in the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
